summary: In this post, we share how NASWA scaled real-time labor market insights using AWS generative AI.
title: How NASWA scales real-time labor market insights with AWS generative AI

This was the first public technical exercise demonstrating the independence of a sovereign cloud Region. The AWS European Sovereign Cloud is a new, independent cloud partition [...]
title: Inside a successful AWS European Sovereign Cloud exercise to demonstrate independent operation

summary: The agentic launches that stayed with me last week had nothing to do with how capable a model is. They were about reach. AWS Step Functions, which already orchestrates over 220 AWS services, can now be handed to an agent as a tool, so workflows teams already trust became callable without a rewrite. In the [...]
title: AWS Weekly Roundup: GPT-6.1 Terra on Bedrock, Step Functions as agent tools, and more (November 2, 2026)

summary: When MySQL commits a large transaction, writing it to the binary log can freeze every other commit on the server for minutes. This post introduces Binary Log Optimization for Large Transactions (BOLT), an AWS contribution to community MySQL that makes commit latency independent of transaction size, speeds crash recovery, and improves throughput.
title: AWS contributes a large-transaction binary log optimization to MySQL

summary: Circle K’s DevOps team cut incident triage from 45-60 minutes to under 15 by building an agentic triage system on Amazon Bedrock. This post walks through the architecture, the initial Amazon Bedrock Flows implementation, the migration to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and the lessons learned from scaling it.
title: How Circle K accelerated DevOps incident triage to under 15 minutes with Amazon Bedrock

summary: Learn how to build a multi-agent engineering assistant that compresses aerospace component substitution evaluation from days to minutes, using Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and the Strands Agents SDK to assemble substitution evidence while keeping the engineer as the decision-maker.
title: Agentic engineering intelligence with Amazon Nova Multimodal Embeddings and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

summary: Agentic assistants built on frontier models run a multi-step tool loop, and paying frontier prices on every step is hard to sustain at production scale. This post shows how to use sequence-level knowledge distillation (SeqKD) to transfer a frontier teacher’s agentic behavior into a small, lower-cost student on Amazon SageMaker AI.
title: Build efficient agents with knowledge distillation on Amazon SageMaker AI

summary: This post shows how to use Crawl4AI, an open source web crawler, as a content preparation layer for Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, handling JavaScript rendering, selective extraction, and custom metadata enrichment before web content reaches an Amazon S3 data source.
title: Prepare web content for Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases with Crawl4AI

summary: Learn how to migrate Google BigQuery workloads to an open lakehouse on AWS built on Apache Iceberg and Amazon S3. This post explains why an open lakehouse future-proofs your data, presents the target architecture on AWS, and walks through a step-by-step migration: assess, design, convert, migrate, cut over, and optimize.
title: Migrate Google BigQuery to an open lakehouse on AWS with Apache Iceberg

summary: Keeping a large Amazon EC2 fleet continuously recoverable with AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery is a lifecycle challenge. This post shows how to automate the full DRS agent lifecycle (install, heal, and offboard) using AWS Systems Manager Automation and Amazon EventBridge, driven by a single EC2 tag and no Lambda functions.
title: Automating the full AWS DRS agent lifecycle: Install, heal, and offboard

summary: A disaster recovery strategy is only as strong as the business decisions behind it. Before you choose an architecture pattern, three decisions shape whether recovery succeeds: what you’re actually recovering, what the business needs from that recovery, and what your dependencies allow you to commit to. Part 1 of a three-part series.
title: Three business decisions that define your DR success

summary: After you define your DR targets, testing tells you whether they hold. This post walks through a four-level progressive validation model (tabletop, planned failover, surprise drill, and game day) and shows how each level surfaces a different class of recovery gap that feeds back into your commitment. Part 2 of a three-part series.
title: Validating your DR commitment: From controlled test to real-world readiness

summary: This final post turns the DR framework into a repeatable engagement: a five-step sequence from kickoff and gap assessment through progressive validation to an updated recovery commitment, with a real before-and-after example and ways to compress the timeline from months to weeks. Part 3 of a three-part series.
title: How to run a DR readiness engagement

title: Beyond DKIM key rotation: understanding email replay attacks

title: Introducing queue consumption mode for Apache Kafka in AWS Lambda

title: Extending AWS DevOps Agent with Skills, Model Context Protocol (MCP) Servers, Custom Agents and Connectors

summary: Banking, financial services, and insurance (BFSI) institutions need AI systems that can act autonomously at market speed, but autonomy without governance is a nonstarter in an industry defined by regulatory intensity and operational risk. In this post, Apexon and AWS present an architecture-first approach to operationalizing agentic AI on AWS, with governance built in from the start across three layers: intelligence, orchestration and execution, and governance, security, and audit. Learn how governed agentic patterns apply to core BFSI workflows like customer onboarding, credit processing, and payments exception handling, enabling autonomy at scale while keeping every action traceable and auditable.
title: Scaling agentic AI for governed banking operations with Apexon and AWS
